target_role: CTO, engineering lead, or de facto compliance owner at a B2B SaaS startup
workflow: Collecting SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audit evidence by hand: screenshots of cloud and IAM configurations, quarterly user-access reviews assembled in spreadsheets, gathering vendor security certificates, tracking policy acknowledgments, and packaging all of it for auditors.
trigger: Scheduled audit windows, quarterly access-review cycles, and enterprise customer due-diligence requests
frequency: quarterly access reviews; annual audits; per-deal security reviews
current_workaround: Manual screenshots stored in shared drives, spreadsheet-based access reviews, or paying for compliance automation platforms (e.g., Vanta, Drata) and compliance consultants; HN discussions frequently debate build-vs-buy and complain about platform pricing.
consequence: Audit delays or failures, blocked enterprise deals, and weeks of senior engineering time diverted to evidence gathering

target_role: Founder, bookkeeper, or finance/operations person at a SaaS or e-commerce company
workflow: Reconciling payment-processor payouts (Stripe, PayPal, Adyen) against individual invoices, fees, refunds, and chargebacks, then getting that data into QuickBooks or Xero; lump-sum payouts must be matched to many underlying transactions.
current_workaround: CSV exports manipulated in Excel or Google Sheets, hand-written reconciliation scripts, paying bookkeepers to do the matching, or buying third-party connector tools that users complain break or mis-map data.
consequence: Books that don't reconcile, misstated revenue, tax filing errors, and several hours of manual work every month

target_role: Sales engineer, solutions engineer, or founder selling to enterprise customers
workflow: Answering bespoke customer security questionnaires (often Excel files with hundreds of questions, or SIG/CAIQ variants) by hunting down previous answers and copy/pasting from old questionnaires and internal documents.
trigger: Each enterprise sales cycle, vendor assessment, or renewal review
frequency: per-deal; multiple per month at companies with active enterprise pipelines
current_workaround: A master answer spreadsheet or document maintained by hand, copy/paste from prior questionnaires, or purchasing questionnaire-automation tooling; HN commenters regularly describe this as one of the most tedious parts of enterprise sales.
consequence: Slower deal cycles, inconsistent or stale answers reaching customers, and senior technical staff consumed by repetitive paperwork

target_role: Backend engineer or operations lead at a SaaS company handling personal data
workflow: Fulfilling GDPR/CCPA data subject requests: locating all of one user's data across production databases, data warehouses, logs, backups, and third-party processors, then deleting or exporting it and documenting completion.
trigger: Each inbound data access or deletion request
frequency: per-request, recurring; spikes after press coverage or policy changes
current_workaround: Hand-written per-request scripts, spreadsheets to track request status and deadlines, and manual checklists for each third-party vendor that holds user data.
consequence: Regulatory exposure, missed statutory deadlines (e.g., 30-day GDPR window), and incomplete deletions discovered later

target_role: Founder or operations lead at a remote-first startup
workflow: Paying international contractors: collecting W-8BEN/W-9 forms, handling currency conversion and wire fees, tracking invoices across countries, issuing 1099s, and staying compliant with each jurisdiction's contractor rules.
trigger: Each pay run, each new contractor onboarding, and annual tax filing
frequency: biweekly or monthly pay runs; annual filings
current_workaround: Manual wire transfers or Wise/PayPal payments tracked in spreadsheets, or paying employer-of-record / contractor platforms (Deel, Remote, Plane) specifically because the manual process is painful; HN threads on this topic recur and discuss misclassification risk.
consequence: Tax penalties, worker misclassification risk, late or incorrect payments, and hours of administrative work per pay run

target_role: RevOps, data engineer, or operations generalist at a growing SaaS company
workflow: Keeping customer records consistent across CRM (Salesforce/HubSpot), billing (Stripe), support tools, and the data warehouse: deduplicating records, fixing drift between systems, and reconciling conflicting metrics like MRR across sources.
trigger: Ongoing data drift, reporting cycles, and disputes between teams over whose numbers are correct
current_workaround: Zapier/Make glue that breaks silently, periodic CSV export/import, internal Python sync scripts that one person maintains, and manual deduplication passes in spreadsheets.
consequence: Conflicting metrics across teams, billing errors, and decisions made on stale or wrong data

target_role: IT admin, office/operations manager, or founder at a startup without dedicated IT staff
workflow: Offboarding departing employees: revoking access across dozens of SaaS tools (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, AWS, and long tails of per-team tools) using a manual checklist, plus rotating any shared credentials the person knew.
trigger: Each employee departure, contractor end, or role change
frequency: per-event, recurring; painful in proportion to headcount churn
current_workaround: Spreadsheet or wiki checklists of accounts, manually clicking through each tool's admin console, or buying identity-governance tooling; HN discussions note that shared accounts and per-team tools are routinely missed.
consequence: Former employees retaining access (a real security incident vector) and orphaned paid seats quietly wasting money

target_role: Small business owner or freelance bookkeeper
workflow: Routine bookkeeping in QuickBooks Online: manual transaction categorization, fixing bank-feed mismatches and duplicates, duplicate data entry between invoicing/payment tools and QBO, and working around missing or regressed features.
trigger: Ongoing bookkeeping work and month-end close
current_workaround: Excel side-ledgers kept in parallel, memorized workarounds, and paying accountants to clean up QBO files; recurring HN threads complain about QBO reliability, UI regressions, and price increases, with users asking for alternatives.
consequence: Books that don't reconcile, accountant cleanup bills, and hours of lost time each month
